clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 613-2136 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10710.txt, 22 FR 3405): signed 1957-05-14; creates under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 a Board of Inquiry of members to be appointed by the President to inquire into the issues in the labor dispute between Goodyear Atomic Corporation and certain of its employees represented by Local 10-689, Oil, Chemical, and Atomic Workers International Union, AFL-CIO, at the Portsmouth Plant of the Atomic Energy Commission near Waverly, Ohio (the order recites that the dispute has resulted in a strike); gives the Board the powers and duties set out in Title II of that Act; directs it to report in accordance with section 206 on or before May 15, 1957; and provides that after the report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as the Act requires until the President terminates it. The May 15, 1957 date is a report deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C, applied to this board-of-inquiry order by analogy; the order's own end is the Presidential termination, which is a contingent event). No instrument terminating the Board, and no board report, is held in the packet or located by the number-citation scan of held texts, so neither a report date nor a Presidential termination is established, and a termination by a Presidential act that is not a held instrument is not excluded; the order is not treated as ended by performance. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10710 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10601 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain contains only EO 12553 where an acting provision is located, and the number-citation scan lists no other later order naming this order.

research_rationale:
EO 10710 creates a Taft-Hartley section 206 Board of Inquiry for an Atomic Energy Commission contractor dispute. Its commands are creation of the board, a report deadline and continuation until the President terminates the board. The report deadline is not an end; no Presidential termination instrument is held; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The caveat that a non-held Presidential act could have terminated the board earlier is stated in the clause reason and is not filled by inference. Searches: no U.S. Code or eCFR hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search adds nothing beyond EO 12553 in the dossier chain.
